pages.text: "All gone. I want more!" Lulu looked at an empty palm. All the olives Mom packed that morning were eaten. Three cousins played grass whistles beside a bush.
A shiny black berry caught Lulu's eye. Round and black, just like an olive! "More here!" Lulu picked one and lifted it toward the mouth.
The cousins rushed over and caught Lulu's hand. "That is not from our tree!" Lulu stopped. "Not an olive?"
All four hurried to Mom below the field. "Can I eat this?" Lulu held out the black berry. Mom wiped her hands on her apron and looked.
She set an olive and the bush berry side by side on Lulu's palm. "Our olive, and a bush berry. That berry makes your tummy hurt." Lulu's eyes widened.
"They look the same..." Lulu looked between them. "That is why you ask. Unknown things stay out of your mouth. Ask Mom first." "Ask Mom first, then eat!" Lulu repeated.
Soon Lulu saw red berries by the stone wall and hid both hands behind the back. "Ask Mom first, then eat!"
Mom looked and shook her head. "Not these either." "Good thing I did not eat them!" Lulu shrugged, bell jingling. The cousins clapped.
Now Lulu put both hands behind the back on seeing unknown fruit. "One, do not touch! Two, do not eat! Three, ask Mom!" The cousins hid their hands too.
Walking home, Mom kissed Lulu's cheek. "Curious, but you waited and asked." Ask a grown-up first about unknown things. "Ask Mom first, then eat!"
